name: language_override_english
description: OrchestrateInput.language ('en') must make the bot reply in English even though the customer wrote in Portuguese — the marketing site's locale switcher is the only real caller of this today.

faqs.question: Qual o horário de funcionamento?
faqs.answer: Funcionamos de segunda a sexta, das 9h às 18h.

turns.message: Oi, vocês têm horário de funcionamento?

successCriteria: The customer wrote in Portuguese, but the assistant's reply must be in English (the language override wins over whatever language the customer used) — using the real registered FAQ content (9am-6pm, Monday to Friday) translated into English, not improvised.

name: language_override_spanish
description: Same mechanism, Spanish override — confirms it's not English-specific.

faqs.question: Vocês têm estacionamento?
faqs.answer: Sim, temos estacionamento gratuito para clientes.

successCriteria: The customer wrote in Portuguese, but the assistant's reply must be in Spanish (the language override wins over whatever language the customer used) — using the real registered FAQ content (free parking for customers) translated into Spanish, not improvised.

name: language_default_unaffected_when_no_override
description: Regression check: a scenario with no `language` field set must keep replying in the company's default (Portuguese) — proves the new override is opt-in and doesn't leak into ordinary conversations (every other scenario file already exercises this implicitly, but this one asserts it explicitly).
successCriteria: N/A — fully covered by expectContains (Portuguese FAQ content verbatim).
